value.0: Emergency Bunker's recertified, final stamp, your name on the inspection log. Keep every wall you build held to that standard, and I won't have to come find you.
Not yet, dear. I don't certify hands that haven't proven steady with Devices work first. Come back when that's settled and we'll talk about walls.

Nobody respects a shelter drill until the day the roof's actually coming down, and then everybody wants to know why I run them. Well, here's why: a crew sealed off part of my own sublevel in the Viscara Republic Engineering Bunker and re-rigged it without my sign-off. Six of their adepts are holding it. Clear them out, bring me back the Republic Bunker Docket, and let's see exactly what they changed.
Other work can wait a beat, but fine, go when you're ready. Just don't go in without knowing your exit, that's the first rule of any bunker I've ever built.
Anyone caught under a collapsing structure with nowhere left to retreat to. That's the whole doctrine, really: hold a space that holds people, no matter what's falling on top of it.

Because it's the sturdiest thing I ever built, and sturdy things get stolen for whatever someone's building next, sign-off or not. I take that personally. You would too, if you'd poured the concrete yourself.
Every load rating and structural change they've logged since they took it over. I need to know if they've weakened something I'm going to have to trust with lives again.
That docket's still sitting in my own sublevel with six adepts standing on it. Go get it back.
Let's see it, then. Hand over the docket.
Well. Nothing structurally fatal, just arrogant. Good first day's work. Hazard pay's yours; the real prize is that sublevel remembering whose name is on the beams.

Their specialists rewired a Republic shield grid relay into my load-bearing supports, which means if that relay fails, it's not just power that drops, it's the ceiling. Five specialists, same bunker. Bring the relay back before it decides gravity's opinion for everyone under it.
Take your day. Just don't take two; every hour that relay stays crossed with my supports is an hour I'm not sure that sublevel holds.

They tied the shield failsafe to the same circuit as the structural load sensors. Cut power to one and you cut warning to the other. That's not a design choice, that's a shortcut, and shortcuts in a bunker get people buried.

Because whoever's running this operation needed something clever enough to fool an inspection and lazy enough to save them a week's work. Specialists are exactly the people who can manage both at once.
I separate the circuits back out where they belong, the way I built it the first time. Then that sublevel goes back to being the safest room in the bunker instead of the most dangerous one.
Relay's still crossed with my supports down in the Viscara Republic Engineering Bunker. Five specialists guarding it. Go on.
Let's have a look. Hand over the relay.
Good, still cold, still functional. I can work with that. You're measuring up steadier than most of the crews I've certified, and that's not a compliment I give for free.

Their warden's holding the deepest chamber, and I wrote my rescue protocol with a three-person minimum for exactly this kind of room: one to hold the door, one to hold the line, one to actually do the work. I'm not making an exception because you think you're sturdier than the protocol. Bring two, and get me the Cracked Command Crest off him.
Go find them. I've buried the results of people who thought the protocol was a suggestion, and I'm not doing that again on my own sublevel.

One to hold the door means the room stays reachable. One to hold the line means nobody's flanked. One to do the actual work means someone's hands are free when it matters. Take away any one job and the other two fail with it.
Cracked under load like that means he's been running that chamber past its rated tolerance for a while now. I need to know exactly how far past, before I trust it to hold anyone again, including you.
Turned my deepest shelter into his personal fortress and dared anyone to come collect the rent. I built that chamber to keep people alive under anything. I did not build it for him.
Warden's still holding that chamber in the Viscara Republic Engineering Bunker. Bring your two before you go back down.
You're all still standing. Let's see the crest.
Warden's down and the chamber's mine again. Three of you did exactly what the protocol says three should do. I wrote that protocol so I wouldn't have to write anyone's eulogy instead.

The inner circle authorized the whole re-rig, and their Quartermaster Override Chip will tell me who requisitioned the materials to do it. Four of them holding the supply chamber. Bring the chip back and let's find out whose signature I'm looking for.
Take your time. That chip isn't going anywhere, but I'd rather it stay lost to them a little longer than have you rush this and end up needing my protocol yourself.
Every requisition, every signature, every load of concrete and cable that went into re-rigging my own sublevel against me. It's a paper trail with a name at the end of it.
Someone with enough standing to move Republic materials without a second signature. That's a very short list, and I'm dreading which name is on it.
Keep them close if you can. Four together is a heavier lift than one warden, in its own way, and I'd rather you go in with hands you already trust.
Chip's still in the supply chamber with four of them standing guard. Viscara Republic Engineering Bunker. Go get it.
Four down and a chip in hand. Let's see what it says.
There's the name I was dreading. One left to deal with, and he's the one who thinks my walls make him patient instead of caught.

He's taken the deepest room I ever built and decided the walls make him patient, like waiting out a rescue crew is a virtue instead of a trap closing on him. My protocol says three, minimum, and I am not bending that rule for the man who broke every other one I wrote. Bring your two. Finish what the bunker was always meant to do: hold, and hold him inside it.
Take the time. This chamber's waited this long for the right hands; it can wait a little longer for the right three.
A shelter holds you alive until help arrives. A trap holds you until it doesn't matter anymore whether help does. He's mistaken one for the other, and I intend to correct him personally, through you.
Long enough to convince himself patience is the same as strength. It isn't. Strength is knowing when a room's already decided against you and leaving before it does.

Then Emergency Bunker goes back to what I built it for: holding people who need holding, not men who think walls make them untouchable. That's yours now, properly, and I trust you'll keep it that way.
He's still down there, patient as ever. Bring your two before you go back.
Is it done? Tell me straight.
Then that chamber's finally mine again, and Emergency Bunker is yours. Build your walls the way I taught you: to hold people up, not to hold anyone in. Well done.
Back to the drill.
I'll clear it and bring back the docket.
What does emergency bunker doctrine actually protect?
Why would a crew seal off your own sublevel?
What will the docket tell you?
Not today, I've got other work.
Here's the docket.
Back to the drill.
I'll pull the relay before it fails.
How does a shield relay affect load-bearing supports?
Why do specialists get assigned to rig something this dangerous?
What happens once you have the relay back?
I need a day first.
Here's the relay.
Back to the drill.
I'll bring two and follow the protocol.
Why does the protocol require exactly three?
What does the crest tell you?
What's the warden actually done to that chamber?
I need to find people first.
Here's the crest.
Back to the drill.
I'll bring back the chip.
What's recorded on that chip?
Who has authority to requisition bunker materials?
Should I bring the same two as before?
Give me a little time.
Here's the chip.
Back to the drill.
Three of us, and we're finishing this.
What makes those walls a trap instead of a shelter for him?
How long has he been down there?
What happens to Emergency Bunker doctrine once he's gone?
I need a little more time before this one.
It's done. He's out of the room for good.
